overview: The foundational distinction in genetics between the genetic code an organism carries and the observable traits that result.
genZNote: Genotype is the recipe. Phenotype is the dish that comes out.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: The complete set of alleles/genetic instructions an organism carries for a given trait or across its genome.
aspects.valueB: The observable physical, biochemical, or behavioral characteristics that result from genotype and environment.

aspects.label: Nature of the Property
aspects.valueA: Fixed at fertilization; encoded in DNA sequence.
aspects.valueB: Can vary even with the same genotype, depending on environmental and developmental factors.

aspects.label: What Determines It
aspects.valueA: Combination of alleles inherited from both parents.
aspects.valueB: Genotype expressed through the lens of environment, epigenetics, and gene interactions.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Having one allele for brown eyes (B) and one for blue (b) — genotype Bb.
aspects.valueB: Actually having brown eyes, because B is dominant over b.

aspects.label: How It Is Assessed
aspects.valueA: Determined by DNA sequencing, PCR-based genotyping, or pedigree analysis.
aspects.valueB: Observed directly — physical examination, biochemical assay, or behavioral assessment.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: The underlying genetic makeup, not directly visible.
aspects.valueB: The visible/measurable expression of that genetic makeup.

overlay.commonMisconception: Identical genotype does not guarantee identical phenotype — environment and gene regulation can change the outcome (e.g. identical twins with different traits).
